MyBoatPlans Review: Can You Build Your Dream Boat With 518 Step-by-Step Blueprints?

Dreaming of building your own wooden sailboat, fishing skiff, or kayak without wasting thousands on confusing blueprints? We review Martin Reid’s massive DIY boat building archive.

There is an undeniable, timeless magic about being out on the open water in a vessel that you crafted with your own two hands. For generations, woodworking and maritime enthusiasts have dreamed of building their own boats. Yet, for most aspiring hobbyists, that dream quickly turns into an expensive, frustrating nightmare.

Why? Because traditional boat building plans available on the market are notoriously cryptic. They often look like they were written in ancient Greek, missing critical measurements, skipping crucial assembly steps, or leaving beginners completely stranded half-way through a project with a half-built hull that cannot be salvaged.

Enter MyBoatPlans. Created by master boat builder and educator Martin Reid, this comprehensive digital library promises to give everyday woodworking enthusiasts access to over 518 illustrated, step-by-step boat plans, video tutorials, and CAD software tools. In this exhaustive, in-depth review, we examine everything included in Martin Reid’s archive, its pros and cons, and whether it can genuinely help beginners build professional-grade watercraft.

The Hidden Pitfalls of Standard Boat Building Blueprints

If you have ever attempted to build a wooden dinghy, canoe, or small skiff using cheap or generic plans found online, you already know the profound agony of vague instructions. You spend your weekends measuring, cutting, clamping, and gluing, only to discover that a critical angle or dimension was omitted.

The worst part? Hearing that inevitable question from your family or friends: "How’s that boat coming along?" Nothing feels quite as disheartening as abandoning a woodworking project because the blueprints lacked clarity, leaving you out of pocket for lumber, epoxy, and fiberglass with nothing to show for it.

Martin Reid experienced this exact struggle firsthand. Growing up with a deep fascination for boats fostered by his father, his early attempts at building ended in failure due to poorly written local shop plans. It required years of mentorship from a master boat builder for Reid to master the craft. Now, after 31 years of professional boat building, he has compiled his entire life’s work into a single, comprehensive system designed to eliminate guesswork entirely.

What Is MyBoatPlans?

MyBoatPlans is not just a single book or a handful of basic sketches. It is a massive, all-inclusive digital archive containing over 518 step-by-step boat plans covering virtually every style and class of watercraft imaginable.

Designed with absolute beginners and seasoned woodworkers alike in mind, the program provides crystal-clear photographs, detailed specifications, exploded views, and comprehensive material lists. Whether you want to build a lightweight kayak for weekend fishing trips, a classic wooden sailboat for coastal cruising, a rugged duck-hunting boat, or a spacious pontoon, the archive acts as a virtual master craftsman looking over your shoulder.

What Types of Boats Can You Build With the Archive?

The sheer diversity of the MyBoatPlans library is staggering. Rather than forcing you into a single style, the collection features detailed plans for:

  • Canoes and Kayaks: Perfect beginner projects that require minimal materials and offer incredible stability on lakes and slow rivers.
  • Fishing Skiffs and Flat-Bottom Boats: Rugged, utility-focused vessels ideal for inland waterways, bass fishing, and marsh navigation.
  • Classic Wooden Sailboats: Elegant daysailers and cruising boats designed for wind-powered maritime adventure.
  • Duck Boats and Hunting Punts: Specialized shallow-draft watercraft built for camouflage and stability in wetland environments.
  • Pontoons and Small Motorboats: Great family watercraft for relaxing weekends on the lake.
  • Rowboats and Dinghies: Traditional tender boats that make fantastic introductory woodworking projects.

What’s Included Inside the MyBoatPlans Package?

When you unlock access to Martin Reid’s system, you receive far more than just static PDF documents. The package is engineered as a complete masterclass in maritime woodworking:

1. Over 518 Comprehensive Boat Plans

Every single plan in the archive comes equipped with step-by-step instructions, precise dimensions, material lists, and high-resolution photographs illustrating key assembly phases.

2. Over 40 Step-by-Step Video Tutorials

Sometimes reading a diagram isn’t enough. The inclusion of 40+ video tutorials allows you to watch a master craftsman demonstrate complex woodworking techniques, scarf joints, fiberglass application, and hull shaping in real time.

3. Custom CAD Software & Design Guides

Want to modify an existing design or sketch your own custom hull? The program includes specialized CAD software and tutorials that empower you to design your dream boat digitally before making a single cut in lumber.

4. Comprehensive Woodworking Guidebooks

From selecting the right marine-grade plywood and epoxies to proper sanding, painting, and finishing techniques, the guides ensure your finished vessel is structurally sound and aesthetically stunning.

The Pros and Cons of MyBoatPlans

To provide a balanced, objective evaluation, let's examine the primary advantages and potential drawbacks of this digital program:

The Pros:

  • Massive Variety: With over 518 plans, you will never run out of projects, whether you want a simple weekend canoe or an advanced sailboat.
  • Beginner-Friendly Clarity: Step-by-step instructions and video walkthroughs make complex boat building accessible to novices.
  • Massive Cost Savings: Building your own boat using wholesale materials costs a fraction of buying a retail watercraft.
  • Instant Digital Access: You can download all plans, videos, and software immediately to your computer, tablet, or smartphone.
  • Customization Freedom: The inclusion of CAD software lets hobbyists tweak designs to fit their exact storage and seating needs.

The Cons:

  • Requires Workspace and Tools: Building a boat requires a dedicated garage, workshop, or shed space, along with standard woodworking tools (saws, clamps, sanders).
  • Time Commitment: Woodworking is a labor of love; building a sturdy watercraft requires patience, precision, and adherence to curing times for epoxies and paints.

Frequently Asked Questions (FAQ)

1. Can a total beginner really build a boat with these plans?

Yes. The archive is specifically structured with projects ranging from ultra-simple canoes and small dinghies for beginners to advanced yachts for experienced woodworkers.

2. How are the plans delivered?

The entire system is digital. Upon enrollment, you get instant login access to download the plans, view the video tutorials, and access the software.

3. Do I need professional woodworking machinery?

Most projects can be built using standard workshop tools like a jigsaw, sander, drill, and hand tools, alongside common safety gear.

Final Verdict: Is MyBoatPlans Worth It?

If you have ever harbored a desire to build your own watercraft without getting bogged down by confusing, incomplete blueprints, MyBoatPlans is an exceptional investment. Backed by 31 years of professional expertise from Martin Reid, it bridges the gap between professional maritime engineering and weekend DIY hobbyism.

With its vast library of 518+ plans, helpful video tutorials, and custom design tools, this archive earns our highest recommendation for woodworkers, fishermen, and boating enthusiasts ready to hit the water in a boat they built themselves.
